subject: Request: staging quarantine and short-term version segregation for Orpheus-mini variant
content:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: staging quarantine and short-term version segregation for Orpheus-mini variant

Team —

Acme ran a limited set of tests against Orpheus-mini-2.7b-v2 yesterday; they reported intermittent hallucination regressions when context includes long system instructions. Marketing is pushing for the variant to go live in sandbox next week, but before we let it touch any shared staging pools I want to request a short-term "segregation + quarantine" for the variant while we finish compatibility checks.

Ask:
- Put orpheus-mini-2.7b-v2 into a dedicated staging pool (no shared KV/cache with other models) for 7 days.
- Pin the variant ID to that pool and prevent automatic routing to host pools used for general testing.
- Run the compatibility smoke tests (attached checklist + compat-smoketests.log) across our standard latency/qa/long-context matrices.

Why: partially reproducible hallucination has a moderate customer impact signal; we want to avoid noisy telemetry affecting other models and avoid accidental routing to prod canaries.

Timeline: If we can start quarantine by Monday 2026-11-09 EOD, that gives reviewers time to run the regression suite and for research to triage.

Dev/Research — can you confirm technical feasibility (blocking changes, ETA, known risks) and ownership for the tests?

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: staging quarantine and short-term version segregation for Orpheus-mini variant

Markus —

We can do the segregation but a few implementation notes:
- Dedicated pool creation: ~3 hours to spin up a small dedicated staging pool (1-2 nodes) and pin variant. I can have infra config changes staged by EOD Monday if approved.
- KV/cache isolation: we'll need to disable global prefix caching for the pool (there's a flag). That will slightly increase token cost for these runs but prevents cross-model contamination.
- Routing rules: policy change to prevent automated fallback will require a short gating CR; ops can apply an explicit allowlist for the pool ID.

Known risk: If the variant uses a different tokenizer or produces longer average token lengths, some of our batching heuristics under constant batcher may mis-estimate, leading to higher tail latency. We'll include a histogram-run in the smoke tests.

I can own the pool creation and routing lock if Jonas owns the regressions and Laura owns customer communication.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:19:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: staging quarantine and short-term version segregation for Orpheus-mini variant

Markus / Dev / Laura —

I ran a quick triage of the logs Acme sent (see compat-smoketests.log). The hallucination pattern looks like prompt-instruction truncation at ~3k tokens when system prompts include nested JSON-like tooling directives. Preliminary hypothesis: model's tokenization of some punctuation sequences produces split tokens that push critical instruction tokens out of the attention window.

Plan for regressions:
- Run full long-context pass (1k / 3k / 6k) with the customer's exact system templates.
- Enable debug KV dump for the runs to capture attention alignment around truncated instructions.
- Compare outputs against v1 (orchid-stable-2.7b) on identical prompts to compute per-token divergence and a hallucination-flag metric.

Canaries: if results show divergence > 0.12 hallucination metric vs v1, we should hold. If lower but non-zero, propose a 48h canary inside the sealed pool with telemetry gating (rate limited, no routing to production).

I can spin the tests tomorrow morning and post results to the Drive folder.

— Jonas
Applied ML — Model Safety & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: staging quarantine and short-term version segregation for Orpheus-mini variant

Thanks all —

From a product standpoint: we should be conservative here. Acme is an important pilot customer and we have to balance speed with safety. My suggested next steps:
1) Approve Dev to create the dedicated staging pool and pin the variant (7-day window).
2) Jonas runs the full regressions and posts the summary + per-prompt diffs to the Drive link in JIRA INF-8273.
3) If divergence < 0.05, move to a 48h sealed canary with no routing to prod and a rollback kill-switch. If 0.05–0.12, extend sealed canary to 96h and add a short-term fallback to orchid-stable-2.7b. >0.12 — hold.
4) I will coordinate customer comms (Alice) and set expectations: no broader sandbox rollout until we pass the canary criteria.

Markus — please confirm scope and whether you want exec visibility on the decision.

Best,
Laura
Director, Product — Serving Platform
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: orpheus_onboard_checklist.xlsx (checklist of integration steps and QA knobs), compat-smoketests.log (triage logs from Acme's run)
